theories.name: Classical Mechanics

dimension_model.state: finite-dimensional phase space for many toy systems

theories.core_claim: Macroscopic bodies can often be modeled through positions, momenta, and deterministic equations of motion.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare: Classical Mechanics (8.01SC)
sources.note: Course material on Newtonian motion, forces, momentum and energy. An educational reference, not a new empirical test.

theories.name: General Relativity
theories.core_claim: Gravity is modeled as the curvature of spacetime sourced by energy and momentum.

sources.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger
sources.note: GW150914 matched a binary black hole merger waveform predicted by general relativity. This reference supports the gravitational-wave example, not every evidence item.

theories.name: Quantum Mechanics
theories.core_claim: Microscopic systems are described by states whose measurable outcomes are probabilistic.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare: Quantum Physics I (8.04)
sources.note: Introductory material on the experimental basis and wave mechanics of quantum physics. Background reading rather than a primary experimental report.

theories.name: Quantum Field Theory
theories.core_claim: Particles can be modeled as excitations of quantum fields, with interactions constrained by symmetries.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare: Relativistic Quantum Field Theory I (8.323)
sources.note: Graduate course on field quantization and applications to particle and condensed matter physics. It does not validate all possible quantum field theories.

theories.name: Standard Model

dimension_model.internal: gauge and flavor degrees of freedom

theories.core_claim: Known elementary particles and three non-gravitational interactions are described by a gauge quantum field theory.

sources.title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson with the ATLAS detector at the LHC
sources.note: ATLAS observed a new boson compatible with the Standard Model Higgs boson. This is one experimental result, not a complete validation of every Standard Model claim.

theories.name: Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics

dimension_model.microscopic: large phase space or state ensemble

theories.core_claim: Macroscopic regularities emerge from large ensembles of microscopic states.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare: Statistical Physics I (8.044)
sources.note: Course material connecting probability, statistical mechanics and thermodynamics. Examples include thermal radiation and electrons in solids.

theories.name: Lambda-CDM Cosmology
theories.core_claim: The large-scale universe is modeled with cold dark matter, dark energy, expansion, and structure formation.

sources.title: Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters
sources.note: Planck CMB data are consistent with the base six-parameter Lambda-CDM model. This does not establish the microscopic identity of dark matter or the nature of dark energy.

theories.notes: Established here means a widely used cosmological model with substantial observational support within its domain, not a settled account of dark matter, dark energy or current cosmological tensions.

theories.name: Quantum Gravity

dimension_model.candidates: strings, loops, holographic descriptions, emergent spacetime

theories.core_claim: A deeper framework should reconcile quantum theory with dynamical spacetime geometry.
evidence: theoretical motivation: consistency between quantum theory and gravity
mathematical proposals: holographic dualities; not direct empirical confirmation

sources.title: The Large N Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity
sources.note: A theoretical proposal for dualities in specific anti-de Sitter settings. It is not direct empirical evidence for quantum gravity or for this project's hypotheses.

theories.notes: Quantum gravity is an active research area. The cited theoretical work does not establish that a candidate describes the observed universe.

theories.name: Observer Information Frame

dimension_model.informational: coordinates of accessible state, uncertainty, and compression
dimension_model.project_role: connects physical theories to knowledge states inside the hyperbook

theories.core_claim: A theory entry can be compared by what information an observer can access, compress, and update.
evidence: no empirical validation; project-local organizing model only
theories.notes: This working model is a project-local way to organize questions about information and observers. It is not an established physical theory; no supporting empirical evidence is claimed.

theories.name: Dimensional Resonance Hypothesis

dimension_model.speculative: different dimension types may couple through shared invariants or compression patterns
dimension_model.guardrail: must not be presented as established physics

theories.core_claim: Some cross-scale regularities may be modeled as resonance between physical, state-space, and information dimensions.
evidence: none yet; project hypothesis seed only
theories.notes: This speculative project-local hypothesis has no supporting empirical evidence, validated mathematical model or confirmed prediction. It is an analogy seed for discussion, not a discovered physical law.
